tenures.bio: Anthony Balboa was born in 1973 to poor Italian parents Giovanni and Zitta. Anthony was oldest of 6 kids (Anthony, Salvatore, Rocco, Andrea, Vita, Silvia). Balboa wents to school and finished high school. Balboa started Boxing illegaly for money when he was 14. He made enough money to support him and his family. Balboa was a amazing boxer and attracted a crowd of rich Italian Working men, who were willing to bet. In 1990, at the age of 17, Balboa joined an even bigger illegal boxing raccet to gain more money for his family. Balboa was a favorite of the men who gathered around to watch the bare knuckles boxing and made triple the money he made in the last 3 years! At the age of 18, this is when Balboa took a turn for the worst. The Mafia was gaining interest in Balboa, and illegal Boxing and wanted a peace of the action. They signed Several underground boxers, and offered Balboa a deal. Balboa left his family for New York. Balboa thought he'd be treated well and fighting in good conditions, but he was wrong, dead wrong. Balboa got his appartment in the ghetto of New York, and was robbed several times. The Fighting was the worst part. The fighters fought in a pit, like a dog fight, in front of crowds of betting men. There was no rules and Many men brought weapons to the Pit. This is where Balboa learned his Shoot fighting skills and learned the lession of Hardcore. Im the 2 years balboa spent in the ghetto he Toughend up and even Started Robbing other people. Some people say the ghetto turns you to stone, they where right. Balboa, a good boy growing up Went to jail in 1993, Balboa Was arrested for assult. balboa got 4 years, but only did two. Balboa got out in the summer of 1995, job less and homeless. Balboa snuck ontp a flight back to Abruzzi. When Balboa returned to Italy and his family, Every thing had changed. His father had died and his mother was getting weaker. Salvatore Was now head of the family. Balboa did not like this. He felt Salvatore was too weak to run the family. Balboa Become the 'pappa' of the family. He took this too seriously. It was a group of working teen agers, who where good people. They knew Anthony Had changed and they didn't like it. After a few month They were tired of Anthony, who has in and out of jail, and spent long hours at the bar. During this time, balboa developed his scene of humor, constantly laughed at his own jokes that not very many people found funny. Salvatore, the mild mannered younger brother, asked Balboa to leave. Surprizing Balboa left. Balboa moved back to New York. Balboa didn't goto the ghetto instead he went to New York City. Balboa tryed a life at several jobs, but they didn't work. By 1998 he was in organised crime. He joined a small Cosa Nostra called 'The Fattoni Family' or the Mafia. Balboa did small crime with them. During the time he deverloped a 'thing' for wrestling. Missing meetings to Watch wrestling. Balboa was the ultimate fan. Balboa was moving up in the Mafia Rankings becoming a Cappo. In 1999 balboa decided he was going to become a wrestler. Balboa went back to Italy to train. But with Balboa's Mafia Success, there was a danger of getting capped, so balboa brought his friend Tony fattoni and his body guards Jimmy and Johnny Fresco, and his booker (Money Management) Chico D'Aruzzi. All 5 trained, but Balboa was the better of the 5 and seemed like a natural. in July of 2000, Balboa left his Mafia buddys behind and signed with NAPWF. balboa's first match was against Rob 'Robzilla' Andrews July 12, 2000. The Rest Is All History...

tenures.bio:
Born Akira Witt, Cianan grew up in New York, having a rather rough child hood, due to his half breed heritage, in a mostly Italian neighborhood. As a child he was picked on, and beat up. Home life wasn't fun either, his father was a workaholic, and his mother was a stay at home Mom, both fought constantly and were verbally, mentally, and physically abusive to young Cianan. His only escape were his heroes of wrestling, which he longed to be.



Cianan's father eventually had a breakdown, after a physical accident enabling him to work. His father went into a deep depression, and fell asleep, before slipping into a coma, leaving Cianan as the sole provider for his home.



This put incredible stress on Cianan and his mother, who got more and more abusive, as Cianan started growing weary with both school and working to support two people at a young age. As soon as he turned 18, he left, never to return home.



Cianan soon made his way to Japan, where he heard wrestling was in high graces at the time. He quickly joined the first fed that he was accepted to and began training. Though, due to his tainted herritage, his training was harsher then normal, but his will to prove them wrong, and earn there respect. His respect for man kind also went down, along with a small bit of bitterness that continued to grow, during his training.



It escaladed to him finishing his training, in high regards, having earned the respect of his tormentors for the past years. 



In his first official match, he let himself slip, and during a tag match, broke his opponents neck, with a brain buster. He was immediately expelled from the promotion.



So, Cianan went back home, to the USA. He struggled through, working with indy fed after indy fed, until coming across CCW. He quickly saw a Transatlantic Title match featuring Kensuke Suzahara, and joined the federation.



After his joining, Kensuke disappeared.



Cianan started off slowly, working a few feuds, and winning a few titles here and there. Coming close to gaining the CCW World Title #1 contenders ship. After failing, he soon grasped onto a strong position that elevated his career, the CCW Commissionership. He gripped it, and started using his power. While, at the same time joining Jesse Ramey, and Enigma in a stable called The Lost Souls. 



Thus, the embarrassment began. Due to problems with Koriann, Jesse started his cross dressing career. Cianan was horrified, and embarrassed at this course of events, and the frustration that he was putting forth more effort then his compatriots. He quickly proved that he could take care of the trash, by powerbombing Jesse Ramey over the ring to his 'death.'



Aghast at his actions, all of CCW was now against him, and Cianan struggled to hold on. He fought person after person scrounging for more control, and to torture the enemies he made. Cianan turned Enigma's own mother against him, and took away his hard-core title. Cianan took Sebastian 'Switchblade' Toomes, Independent Title, and handed it over to Kyle 'Velocity' Lamen. He took Jason McAllister out of CCW. All the while, constantly being compared to Kensuke Suzahara, which drove him mad. He was obsessed with proving himself better than Kensuke.



His chance came. Kensuke, and his friend Fanatik, finally came back to CCW after long absences. Cianan finally had his chances, but unable to get his hands on Kensuke, due to presidential restrictions. Kensuke won the world title, and the president.. Disappeared.



Cianan grasped the reigns of CCW, and immediately took ultimate control. After losing a harsh match to Enigma, which nearly left Cianan crippled, he was challenged by Kensuke to a #1 contenders match. Cianan accepted, to a Singapore cane on a pole match, which ended quickly, with Kensuke's former girlfriend turning on him, and joining Cianan as a lover.



Cianan had his title shot, but quickly lost in a submission match to Kensuke, which sent him over the edge. He was the submission wrestler, not Kensuke, it hurt his pride.



Cianan hounded Kensuke, and finally got Kensuke in another match for the title.. A 60 Minute Iron Man Match. This time, Cianan came through for himself, and half crippled Kensuke and himself, winning the title.



After a small embarrassment, losing the title on his first defense, He manipulated it back into his hands, without having to fight for it, and using the rule book. 



Cianan had everything. Soon, he had nothing. During a title defense against long time rivals Blayze and Enigma, a spot was blown (or not.) and Cianan's neck was broken, he fought on, and won his defense. But, quickly he was out, and emotionally torn, as his love, announced that she was pregnant.

tenures.bio: Kevin Sandusky was born in Tucson AZ in 1983.. Even before his birth, he was a center for controversy in the wrestling world.. His father, Mark Sandusky, was an up and coming face in the Arizona based SWA.. His mother Rachel Doyle was a 17 yr old girl that worked for the promotion as a seamstress.. Unfortunately for all involved, Mark was already married.... Before Kevin's birth (infact shortly after his conception), Mark was forced out of the SWA by Rachel's father Jack, and her brother Joey (who at the time was a teenage phenom sidekick to 'Mighty' Mark Sandusky) in a move that crippled Mark's marriage and US career.. A divorced, depressed, and desperate Mark Sandusky traveled to Japan in hope that he could find success without the specter of his past hanging over him.. In Japan, Mark was forced to play the 'ugly American' heel.. Isolated in the foreign environment, Mark began to live his gimmick.. The 260 pound Sandusky swelled up to 320 pounds in a lifestyle that was encompassed by the 'Triple S'.. Sake, Sapporo, and Steroids... 'Mad' Mark was a legitimate draw for a time, until his temper started to wear through.. He was pegged as a risky prospect with a penchant for hurting other workers, but was still one of the top 5 'overseas' heels in Japan.. Kevin's uncle Joey continued to work in the SWA... Joey became a father of sorts to Kevin during his early years, as Rachel and Kevin continued to live in the family's home in Tucson.. Joey watched Kevin with a close eye, praying that his father's immoral tendencies wouldn't be passed on to the next generation.. But as with all young men, the future loomed large for Joey Doyle.. Desperate to have a career in the wrestling industy, was forced to leave the US where his cruiserweight style wasn't appreciated, and went to the only place where he could find work.. Japan.. For years Joey and Mark avoided each other in Japan.. Joey being forced into a role as a 'Masked Luchadore' and Mark as a mid-level 'monster-heel'.. The situation was a powder keg, and the fuse was lit in April of 1989 at the Tokyo-Dome.. Mark and Joey were booked against each other.. The Japanese bookers of the event had no idea of what they had done.. They were was shocked and disgusted as Japanese fans and the rest of the world at what came to pass.. What was supposed to be a filler match to bring about a top-level face run-in, turned into a bloodbath... Mark pounded away at Joey mercilessly, until the younger and quicker Joey brought his speed and expertise to bear.. Joey destroyed Mark's knee with a straight kick that bent Mark's knee at a 90 degreee angle, outward.. Worse yet, Joey unmasked, exposing himself as a caucasian and not the Mexican luchadore he was billed as.. Both Mark and Joey left Japan disgraced; both labelled as stupid Americans not professional enough to to what they were told... Ok, back to young Kevin... While this was playing out on the far side of the Pacific, Rachel Doyle fell in love with a part-time SWA trainer, Jose Gonzales.. They eventually married.. Young Kevin was emmersed in the business from the time he could walk.. He showed alot of promise, but also the egotistical arrogance that was so much a part of his father.. He was smug and cocky, and remained that way until one night, Jose set him down and told him the entire story of Rachel and Joey Doyle, Mark Sandusky, and how Kevin came to be... From that night on, Kevin's demeanor changed.. He was focused not to become the wreck of a man that his father became.. He also vowed to right the wrongs that had preceded him.. tenures.bio:
Kevin Sandusky was born in Tucson AZ in 1983.. Even before his birth, he was a center for controversy in the wrestling world.. His father, Mark Sandusky, was an up and coming face in the Arizona based SWA.. His mother Rachel Doyle was a 17 yr old girl that worked for the promotion as a seamstress.. Unfortunately for all involved, Mark was already married....

Before Kevin's birth (infact shortly after his conception), Mark was forced out of the SWA by Rachel's father Jack, and her brother Joey (who at the time was a teenage phenom sidekick to 'Mighty' Mark Sandusky) in a move that crippled Mark's marriage and US career.. A divorced, depressed, and desperate Mark Sandusky traveled to Japan in hope that he could find success without the specter of his past hanging over him..

In Japan, Mark was forced to play the 'ugly American' heel.. Isolated in the foreign environment, Mark began to live his gimmick.. The 260 pound Sandusky swelled up to 320 pounds in a lifestyle that was encompassed by the 'Triple S'.. Sake, Sapporo, and Steroids... 'Mad' Mark was a legitimate draw for a time, until his temper started to wear through.. He was pegged as a risky prospect with a penchant for hurting other workers, but was still one of the top 5 'overseas' heels in Japan..

Kevin's uncle Joey continued to work in the SWA... Joey became a father of sorts to Kevin during his early years, as Rachel and Kevin continued to live in the family's home in Tucson.. Joey watched Kevin with a close eye, praying that his father's immoral tendencies wouldn't be passed on to the next generation..

But as with all young men, the future loomed large for Joey Doyle.. Desperate to have a career in the wrestling industy, was forced to leave the US where his cruiserweight style wasn't appreciated, and went to the only place where he could find work.. Japan..

For years Joey and Mark avoided each other in Japan.. Joey being forced into a role as a 'Masked Luchadore' and Mark as a mid-level 'monster-heel'.. The situation was a powder keg, and the fuse was lit in April of 1989 at the Tokyo-Dome.. Mark and Joey were booked against each other.. The Japanese bookers of the event had no idea of what they had done.. They were was shocked and disgusted as Japanese fans and the rest of the world at what came to pass.. What was supposed to be a filler match to bring about a top-level face run-in, turned into a bloodbath... Mark pounded away at Joey mercilessly, until the younger and quicker Joey brought his speed and expertise to bear.. Joey destroyed Mark's knee with a straight kick that bent Mark's knee at a 90 degreee angle, outward.. Worse yet, Joey unmasked, exposing himself as a caucasian and not the Mexican luchadore he was billed as.. Both Mark and Joey left Japan disgraced; both labelled as stupid Americans not professional enough to to what they were told...

Ok, back to young Kevin... While this was playing out on the far side of the Pacific, Rachel Doyle fell in love with a part-time SWA trainer, Jose Gonzales.. They eventually married.. Young Kevin was emmersed in the business from the time he could walk.. He showed alot of promise, but also the egotistical arrogance that was so much a part of his father.. He was smug and cocky, and remained that way until one night, Jose set him down and told him the entire story of Rachel and Joey Doyle, Mark Sandusky, and how Kevin came to be...

From that night on, Kevin's demeanor changed.. He was focused not to become the wreck of a man that his father became.. He also vowed to right the wrongs that had preceded him.. To prove that a man can overcome his own circumstances and prevail.. But to do that, Kevin went to the one place where he would have to work the hardest to overcome the past.. Japan..

In Japan, Kevin became one of the breakout stars of the new PURE promotion, climbing the ranks and garnering the full support of the initially hostile Japanese fans. As PURE's finacial situation crumbled, Kevin realized he had achieved his goals in Japan. He had overcome the adversities left for him, and he decided to look for work in the states, seeking acceptance not for his father or uncle but for himself. Now Kevin fights for his own career and to expose the American fans to the traditions of lucha and puroresu, to which he owes so much.

tenures.style: 'Kin Kyu Hyaku Kyu Ju Ku Shiki', or the Forbidden 999 Style. It's an unorthodox method of battle that has been developed by Inphino through his relentless training. Training in this style left Inphino amazingly agile and swift, his martial arts talent only becoming more sharp to strike and heavy in defense. His agility allows him the capability to flip back and forward out of suplexes of various types, as well as flip out of DDTs and twist and turn his body in various ways to avoid and/or aim in mid air. The stylish, 'Urban Gothic/industrial' Japanese movement of the same name was roughly based from his unique methods and motives.
tenures.manager: Mina de Margo. She is a Japanese raised in America by adoption, her real name Minako Shirato. She is very stylish and urban, though she consorts with Inphino, who tends to shun away from trends and such. Think of a Japanese girl raised as a rocker/ grunge girl with style. She constantly classifies herself as Inphino’s friend, but nothing is declared. But don’t let her looks fool you, she has some fighting skills under her belt as well. She wears a pair of blue hip hugger jeans with a white belly shirt under a red mesh see through long sleeved shirt. Visible around her hips is her red thong, and her nails are black. Her hair is blood red with a black bandana across her forehead. And her facial features are beautifully seductive, reddish-brown lips and dark eyes.
tenures.finisher: The Forbidden Triad: ==1== Black Dragon Smasher ==2== Lullaby Spike ==3== My Angelic Suicide — ==1== Front headlock to single arm underhook rotating reverse mat slam in kneeling position w/ head in between knees. (Black Dragon Smasher). ***Trademark Finisher*** ==2== Blitz reaches around to lock on a sleeper hold, but jabs his thumb into the opponent’s throat to block the windpipe as he chokes him out. ***Surprise Finisher*** ==3== Blitz goes up to the top rope, presses his palms together in a prayer fashion, and flies off with a 360-rotating Swanton Bomb. ***Extreme Style Finisher***

entrance_music.verbatim: The lights all-lower in the arena, and the fans immediately go into applause and cheer. They all clap their hands in unison for the entrance of Inphino Blitz. Their cheers lower as silence fills the arena. Then from out of nowhere, a mellow beat plays through the speakers, blue lights flashing moderately to the music. Then suddenly, smoke fills the entrance way as hard guitars roar out, and Dragon Ash’s “Glory” breaks into full beat. From out of the smoke walks Inphino Blitz, with Mina de Margo by his side. The people all stand to their feet and cheer as he bows his head, his hand going up in a single palm prayer position. Then he and Mina dash towards the ring, sliding in and climbing up on the turnbuckles. Mina de Margo blows a kiss to the fans as Inphino claws his hands at his face and roars at the people. Mina stands by Inphino as he comes down, and the two of them stare at their opponent(s) across from them. After introduction, Blitz steps forward and bows his head as the entire arena calls out “BLITZ!!” Mina de Margo takes Blitz’s coat and sunglasses and steps out of the ring after tapping knuckles with him.

signature_moves: Taunt: 'Howl of the Black Winds'--- Inphino holds his head back and raises his hands to his face with his hands clawed. He closes his eyes as if he is listening to something, before lowering his head and balling up his fists before his face, opening his eyes to show the usual focused expression he shows during battle. ==1==Shadow Moon: Standing front flip Axe kick, followed by a standing moonsault kick to the opponent already leaning forward. ==2== Sado/Mado---(Sadism/Masochism): Inphino picks opponent up in a Tombstone Piledriver position, but then elevates opponent to a horizontal position before powerbombing him down on the back of his head (Reverse Jacknife Powerbomb). Then he grabs the opponent's legs, rolls him over, and executes a sitdown Electric Chair Drop. ==3== Koto Zuki In---(Koto Moon Negative): Inphino hooks his arm around the front of the opponent's neck from behind, and then hooks the leg. Then he lifts him up and delivers a reverse Fisherman Buster onto the front of the head. Bridging is optional. ==4== Koto Zuki You--- (Koto Moon Positive): An inverted Fisherman Buster. Bridging is optional. ==5==Orochi Nagi---(Mowing Serpent): A running attack where Inphino comes with a spinning wheel kick, but uses his left leg to kick at the back of the knees of the opponent. Therefore, both kicks force the opponent down on the mat, folding him so that his legs are swept from under him and his head bounces off the mat at the end of the kick. ==6== Sanrai No Fujin---(Three Sided Defense): An attack set where the opponent throws a punch, but Inphino blocks and delivers a qucik chop to the face. The opponent punches again, but Inphino blocks again and counters with another hard chop. Then he beckons him forward and yells, 'Ikuze!' (Let's go!). The opponent kicks at him, but this time Inphino grabs the leg, steps over with his leg, and delivers a spinning heel kick to the face, yelling out 'Yoshaa!' (I did it!'). ==7==Rainbow Knocker: One of Inphino's unorthodox 'Forbidden 999' style maneuvers where he turns his back on the opponent, bends back, and grabs his opponent's throat. Then he flips back and hits him in the bridge of the nose with a flipping back kick. ==8==Rewind: (Reverse Rana) Inphino leaps on the foe's shoulders from behind and flips back like he was doing a normal Hurricanrana. The opponent flips backwards onto the back of his head and folds over with his stomach in his face. ==9==Last Retort: The opponent whips Inphino into the ropes. He bounces back and Kung Fu Rolls over the opponent. When the foe turns around, Inphino moonsaults over the opponent, grabs his head in mid air, and drives him down with a diving reverse DDT. ==10==Black Dragon Wave: Inphino runs at the opponent inside the ring. Then he leaps up in a front flip and smashes into the upper body of the foe in a Swanton Vertical Splash. The impact knocks the foe over onto his back, with Inphino landing on his feet behind him. Can also be used for an over the top rope attack. ==11==The Swift: A barraging blur of palm thrusts towards various pressure points of the body, ending with a solid strike to the solar plexus, causing the opponent to drop down on all fours in pain at Inphino's feet. ==12==Bushido Blitz: Blitz runs at the opponent and holds both forearms at his forehead. Then he leaps forward and collides into the opponent's forehead. As the foe falls back, he flies overhead and rolls to his feet. Can be used in springboard fashion, as well as top rope. ==13==Black Dragon Dive: A double Jumping Knee, where Inphino runs and leaps up with both knees pulled up at his waist. The move knocks the opponent over while he lands crouched on his heels. ==14==Horizon Dive: A running facecrusher into the turnbuckle, where Inphino leaps over the top rope to add more force to the move. He lands on the outside and yells out to the fans. ). ==15== Shajitsu No Odori: English ('Dance of Illusion') == Picks opponent up in a Michinoku Driver and spins him around in a 360. Then as he jumps to deliver the move, he shifts the opponent's head around to change the move into an elevated reverse DDT ==16== The Brink of Chaos : A Shooting Star Leg Drop, where Inphino flips off the turnbuckle with his arms stretched out like a swan dive. Then he flips back over and nails the leg drop onto the prone opponent’s throat. Tribute Collection ===For every man Inphino has pinned, he takes their techniques to pay honor to their bout, and modifies it to symbolize the progression made from their fight. ===Lotus Eclipse: (Dark Lotus) Inphino locks in a Guillotine Choke, then rotates so that the opponent stretches across his shoulder with the hold still applied. Then he flips forward for a sitdown Dominator with the choke still applied. Impact, not Submission. ===OKIKI Special:(Taki Nazaki, Team OKIKI) A holding elevated Dragon (Full Nelson) Drop into a Dragon Suplex. ===Enter the Dragon:(Bruce Lee) While Blitz has never faced the legendary Lee, tribute must be given. Therefore Inphino flies at the opponent with a flying sidekick just as the immortal Lee.
tenures.bio: Inphino Blitz is a well defined martial artist usually seen wearing black martial arts slacks, black boots, and a tight black spandex shirt that covers most of his neck. His shoulder length hair is dark blue and black, and usually hangs over his face slightly, covering a portion of it, but he randomly tosses in streaks of color given the mood. Often he is seen wearing a black cloak around his shoulders. His eyes are dark gray, and his handsome face is usually solemn and brooding. His nails are painted black. Inphino is a wandering loner martial artist with a mysterious background and a strive to train and enhance his fighting technique. He's one of the breakthrough Japanese figures to introduce the 'Kin Kyu Hyaku Kyu Ju Ku Shiki' or the 'Forbidden 999 Style' into the Japanese culture. The Forbidden 999 Style, named for Inphino's martial arts form, is the equivalent to the Gothic movement over in the states. There have been many tales and stories telling about the Black Dragon Master. But there has yet to be any opportunity or chance to ask him if any of them are true. Inphino was one who grew up outside of modern society, dwelling in a secluded dojo until he was eighteen. Then from there he traveled the earth for battle, gaining many accolades as well as nurturing and developing his Forbidden 999 Style. Then he found Primetime Wrestling Academy, an institute of training in the US. After a few days, he was brought into Primetime Championship Wrestling alongside Ketsueki Karasu to form Hyakuhei. Later in his three-month career, he teamed with Miyagawa, Kensuke Suzahara, and Ming to form the Elements. In three months, he elevated from tag team specialist to World title contender through the 64-man tournament, the quickest rise through the rankings for any wrestler in PCW history. But then tragedy struck... Inphino was forced out of his title run as well as his position in PCW by one man... Akira Akiyama... Akiyama had devised a scheme to lure Inphino Blitz back to Japan, where the dark forces called the Void Elements were there waiting for him. He was presumed dead to the world, and Akiyama took his claim to his position within PCW. But little to their dismay that the Black Dragon Master was not entirely dead. The details are foggy, but Inphino somehow escaped death, and reclaimed his work visa so that he could return to the USA. By this time, Akiyama had become PCW Extreme Champion...so Inphino congratulated him...and moved on with his life. He found a small Indy federation called Hardcore Championship Wrestling, where he took his time to train, renew and raise his skills even further...waiting for the one day to return into PTC...and hopefully PCW. He is a silent man...but also an honorable and respectable one. He always shakes the hands of his opponents, and also helps them up after he has defeated them. But don't let that make you think he's a nice guy. He's extremely dark and hardly shows emotion. If he shows any, it's usually rage or anger...the sorrow that he shows can hardly be called an emotion since he always seems to be saddened. tenures.bio: Appearance: Joey is 6'4' tall, and weighs in at 227lbs. He has shoulder length blonde hair (natural...not bleached) that rests at the bottom of his neck. He is a well built character, with an immense lower body strength, which he uses to his advantage to break submission holds. Attire: Joey normally wrestles in a pair of baggy black pants (similar to the ones Tajiri wears) with the name 'FLASH' in gold writing down the left leg in English, and down the right leg in Japanese. He also wears a tight black t-shirt with high-cut sleeves (midway up his biceps) His attire is complete by black tape around his wrists. Outside the ring, he wears casual clothes, or, on live shows, his ring attire and a black leather overcoat. History: Born in 1973 in Bradford, England, Joseph Mark Wilson was raised by his mother and father in a posh neighbourhood of the city. Mark Wilson (Joseph's father) worked as an Assistant Manager for an electronics firm, and just three months after Joseph's third birthday, was offered a new job for a fast rising company in Japan. He took the offer. Joseph spent his childhood years growing up in Urawa, just outside Tokyo. Joseph spent his school years learning the Martial Arts, but never really excelled in any of them. Just after his 12th birthday, on the 9th of March 1985, Joseph had an encounter with a sport he could not forget. The Road Warriors had their first Japanese match on the first puroresu card ever held at Ryogoku Kokugikan (Sumo Hall) promoted by All Japan, and Joseph was in attendance. To say that one night changed his life may be a little over-estimating, but it went a long way in helping achieve his future. By the age of 19, Joseph, now known to his Japanese friends as Joey, had decided, after seven years of watching major companies across Japan and on nationalised television networks, that he wanted to join the art of puroresu. After training in his school years in Martial Arts, and in an American wrestling class, Joey knew that he could at least perform the basics that he had seen week in, week out. Applying for a dojo in Urawa, Joey spent a lengthy 9 months learning the ropes, and gaining confidence, experience and knowledge of the art. On the 17th of November, 1992, Joey Wilson debuted on an IOD show in Morioka, wrestling against a much more experienced Mexican wrestler, El Soldado Enmascarado, and lost via a Dragon Suplex in just under 10 minutes. Undeterred, Joey plugged away, assuming a Japanese name (Shi'gurya Keji) and wrestling under a mask for BWA, IOD and various independent groups in Japan. 6 years later, and with a lot of experience behind him, Joey travelled to Mexico, and began to work independents to gain experience in the Lucha Libre style. Wearing his mask as Shi'gurya Keji, he debuted in LLI against a touring Super Crazy, beating him with a Gord Buster in 8:07. In the meantime, Joey had attended various tours and independent shows in England, wrestling under his real name. His last appearance was two weeks after his LLI debut, losing to Alex Shane via Show Stopper in 16:35. The LLI organisers decided to unmask Joey, but still didn't like the name Joey Wilson. Joseph quickly compromised, and the name 'Lightning Kid' was assumed for his two year stint in Mexico. LLI and FMV were the two main benefactors of his talent, however appearing on various tours and independents, Joey gained a lot of experience from fusing the Lucha Libre and puroresu styles together, along with a natural ability in submission based wrestling. In the year 2000, an offer came through from a new promoter in America, the XCWF, for Joey to wrestle under the name Joey Flash. Joey accepted, and flew out to Oregon for the first card, using the Lightning Strikes variation of the Gord Buster to pick up numerous wins. Remaining undefeated, and picking up an award for Match Of The Year from the XCWF fans for a ladder match against Thomas Raine (Joey winning with a variation on Akinori Tsukioka's Moonlight Bomb in 30:23) Joey left the company in a mass exodus when new owners took over and refused to cover wages. 2001, Primetime Championship Wrestling opened its doors to an academy. PWA not only taught people the wrestling basics, but also the 'American style' of 'microphone skills' and 'promo techniques.' Joey never graduated PWA, dropping out for the lack of true sportsmanship he had experience in Japan and Mexico. Apart from a brief appearance in NTICW, Joey worked the British scenes under both aliases (Joey Flash and Shi'gurya Keji), before word was passed about a new era opening in Japan. Joey watched as PURE established itself in Japan, before shutting its doors early in its run. Re-opening under new management opened applications to PURE, and Joey was granted a roster space, again under a mask as Siena. Recent happenings have caused Joey to revert back to the name Joey Flash in PURE, but only time will tell if it's good enough for him to make a name for himself again in Japan.

tenures.bio:
The man who goes by the name of Jordan X Shabazz was actually born Jordan Andrew Copeland. his middle name is taken from his older brother Andrew Copeland, who wrestles in the OSW under the name of Drew Hostyle. Jordan was born in Brooklyn, New York, but after his father left as a child, he was forced to be put up for adoption. He was adopted by a white family in Toronto, Ontario Canada. And Jordan lived in Canada for most of his life. He got good grades and was a very respectful young man. When Jordan graduated from High School, his adopted parents sent him away to The University Of Toronto, perhaps the best University in all of Canada. Jordan studied Broadcast Journalism and graduated with honors. After graduating from University, Jordan took all the money he had saved up from working in a Nestle chocolate Factory, and he moved out on his own. He was at a lost. He didn't know what to do with his life, he got a job with a local radio station called Kiss 92 FM. After spending a few months there, Jordan realized he wasn't liked by some of the people working there. After getting into an altercation with one of the DJs Jordan physically assualted him and accidently killed him. They tried Jordan for involuntary Manslaughter. That's where he met his friend, and current manager, Jake Jackson. Jordan was facing a life sentence in prison, but he convinced his manager that it was Self-Defense, and Jake Jackson, used his brain, and he made sure Jordan got off by paying some of the jury members. Jordan walked out of court a free man, and that began the bond that those two men share to this very day. After getting out of court, and starting over again with a clean slate, Jordan decided to move back to New York. This time not in Brooklyn, but in Queens. After seeing his brother Drew Hostyle for the first time in over 15 years, the two men shared a bond. Drew was a professional wrestler, and he encouraged Jordan to join the profession. Jordan did. Jordan was trained by legendary wrestling superstar Johnny Rodz. Jordan learned all the tricks and secrets of wrestling. Jordan begin travelling all across America, Canada, Japan, Europe, and Mexico wrestling for very little money. After a wrestling federation he wrestled for closed down in Japan, Jordan moved back over to America, and he got involved in the American wrestling scene. After taking some advice from Drew Hostyle, Jordan went in the Primetime Wrestling Academy and he bettered himself as a wrestling superstar. 



After spending a month and a half in the Academy, Jordan got promoted to the NTICW. In the NTICW, Jordan started off as a nobody, he wasn't known, and he wasn't given his just desserts. Then, one day, he was listening to his radio, and he heard The Phantom Booker on PTC Malice. Jordan called in, and the rest was history. Jordan screamed, ranted, and raved, then he used his radio show popularity to ride his way through the NTICW. Jordan is a regular guest of the Phantom Booker and Brain Chapman on the PTC's Sunday radio show.



While in the NTICW, Jordan feuded originally with Mark Makonie. The two men engaged in an intense feud which included such gimmick matches as a Billy Club match, a no DQ match, and burn the flag match. The latter match was the last match Jordan ever had in the NTICW, he was defending his Extreme Championship against Makonie. In a brutal 30 minute classic, Jordan prevailed, defeating Mark Makonie for a second time, while losing zero times to Makonie. That ended their feud, and Jordan's career in the NTICW. 



The next week, Jordan called into the PTC Malice show like normal, and he begged Xavier Kannon for a job on air. He smothered Xavier with compliments, and after making Jordan look like an ass. He was given a chance to become Xavier Kannon's lackey.



Jordan was supposed to lick somebody's ass for the PCW contract, he was willing to do it, until he realized that the person who's ass he was supposed to kiss was Neo Nazi, and black man hater, Mark Makonie. Jordan immediately refused, which was going to enduce a beating he wouldn't soon forget...But, thankfully, Duke Williams came out to make the save. After Duke and Jordan cleaned house, Duke offered Jordan a chance to become a member of the Malice Crew, Jordan immediately accepted and joined Duke Williams, Rush Mason, Jason Core, and Legend Inc. in that stable.



Jordan originally wrestled under the name of Jordan Crazy, but he changed his name to be one with himself, and to remember his African roots. 



Jordan became a Civil Rights Extremist after being stopped in Miami, Florida for a traffic violation. Jordan felt that the stop was racially motivated, so he began to fight for his people, and a hatred for racist white people developed.



Jordan recently moved to Dallas, Texas to get away from what he thought of 'The Ghetto.'



Jordan decided to try his luck in PURE after watching a match between The Great Muta and Jushin Lyger.



Jordan recently started his own Civil Rights Organization called N.I.G.G.A, Negores International Growing Group Association.

tenures.bio:
History
Kensuke Suzahara made his debut in CCW, expected to be nothing more than a gimmicky Japanese-gimmicked character with some martial arts skill to put over the established talent in CCW. He was Johnny Flame, destined to be nothing more than a comedy wrestler. An enhancement talent. A kid. Life's funny like that. Kensuke pulled up his boots, and managed to become a living legend in CCW, due to his demeanor as an old-school face. He formed the New Strangers, one of the longest-running stables in sports entertainment, and had MANY memorable feuds and title reigns. CCW entered an interfed called FedWars. Immediately, Alexander Miyagawa and Johnny Flame sought each other out, as they were two of the minority of Japanese wrestlers in the United States. A brutal war of words ensued, sparking off a bitter feud that would send Kensuke over to PCW first as Miya's ally...but later, as his enemy. He was fired shortly after their match at 'Back To Old School.' Reappearing a few months later, after an injury in CCW sent him packing, Kensuke went on a winning streak unparalleled in CCW history. At Group Therapy 2001, Kensuke won the CCW Heavyweight Title to the approval of millions of fans. But that's just not enough sometimes. Since then, Kensuke has been discontent with his lot in life, as while loved, he still did not get enouugh respect from the 'boys' backstage. Yet he still played to the fans that adore him. But recently...things have gone wrong. He lost the CCW Heavyweight Title to an archnemesis, Cianan. His most hated enemy, Neurosis came back, and usurped him as the biggest babyface in CCW. His girlfriend left him. And John Jupiter prevented him from going down in CCW history as the first ever Universal Champion. Backstage at CCW's pay-per-view event Irish Spring, Kensuke brutalized his tag team partner, Kyle 'Velocity' Lamen with a chair, and gave him his finishing move, the Stranger, onto an open chair. Kyle's wrestling career is over. Currently suspended from CCW. Currently in possession of a VERY MEAN streak. And in PURE for two reasons. (1) To get revenge on his former stablemates, the Elements (Miyagawa & Inphino Blitz). (2) To get back at the fans of Japan for 'turning on him,' he intends to prove success is his birthright, even though the business has been 'bad' to him. He is the messiah for the disenfranchised, the modern-day Hamlet. The most loved susperstar in CCW history is destined to become the most hated in PURE history. Do you think you can stop him? He doesn't. And neither does Alexander Miyagawa, the owner of PURE. Because Alexander has been taken out of commission, after Ikusa I. Who controls PURE? Kensuke does.
Description
Coming soon. Until then, check out the poser.
Finisher
The Stranger - Inverted Crucifix into Tombstone Piledriver Kensuke lifts his opponent up from underneath both of their arms, while facing away from them (easily done out of inverted facelock position, with Kensuke as the victim). He holds the opponent overhead in an inverted crucifix, then pulls the opponent down in front of him. Kensuke puts the victim's head down between his legs so the victim is up side down and belly to belly with Kensuke. He drops to a sitting position, driving the victim's head into the mat.
Set-Up Moves/Secondary Finishers
Silver Silencer - Leg Lever Takedown with Leg Drop The victim is standing but bent forward. Kensuke stands to the victim's side and hooks the victim's near arm. He puts the leg which is closest to the victim's arm over the back of the victim's neck and hooks it by bending his leg. Kensuke then pulls his leg back and pushes the victim's arm forward in the opposite direction. The victim is then spun sideways and lands flat on their back on the mat. As the victim is falling, Kensuke drops down with a leg drop onto the victim's neck. The Falling Star - Inverted Facelock Swinging Neckbreaker Kensuke applies an inverted facelock on the victim. He quickly spins to a side, wrenching the victim's neck and dropping them face first into the mat. Kensuke gets more height on his jump than most others who perform this move.
Signature Moves
The Dreamstealer - Drop Toe Hold into STF with Double Arm Lock Kensuke drops down to the mat hooking the leg of the victim with one foot in front of the victim's ankle and then trips the victim down by pushing with their other leg on the back of the victim's legs. Then, Kensuke grabs the victim's foot and bends it up. He lies on his side, his bottom leg is behind the victim's knee, and hi top leg is hooked around the victim's shin/ankle. Kense throws the victim's near arm in between his legs and scissor locks the arm and the victim's ankle. He reaches across the victim's chest with one arm and around the victim's free arm and locks his hands around the victim's head. The end result has Kensuke pulling back on the victim's neck, one of the victim's arms is trapped in a leg scissor, the other arm is trapped between Kensuke's chest and under his top arm which is applying the face lock on the victim. Mask Of The Angel - Off The Top Rope Shooting Star Mat Slam Kensuke and his victim face each other, Kensuke atop the top turnbuckle, and the opponent standing on the mat. Kensuke does a backflip off the top rope, and as he is landing, he grabs the opponent by the back of the head, and drives his face into the mat as he lands in a sitting position. Star Cycle - Running Super Forward Rolling Fallaway Slam Kensuke lifts the victim up so they are laying stomach first across the his shoulders (a standing fireman's carry). He then runs, leaps, leans forward and slams the victim down and then rolls over them with his own weight. Wind Element Suplex - Belly-to-Back Double Chickenwing Suplex with Bridge Kensuke applies a double chickenwing on the victim and links his hands together behind the victim's back. He then lifts the victim up and holds him there for a moment, putting pressure onto the shoulder blades. Then, Kensuke falls backwards, dropping the victim on their shoulders/neck/upperback. Then, he bridges for a pin. The Strike - 180 Springboard Spear Kensuke leaps to the second rope, and as he comes off, spins 180 degrees and dives at a standing victim. He grabs both their legs, causing the victim to fall backwards to the mat. Disenfranchiser - Half Nelson Standing Mat Slam Kensuke stands behind the victim. He reaches under one of the victim's arms with one hand and places it behind the victim's neck. Then, Kensuke grabs the victim by his neck with his free hand and slams their face into the mat.
Stolen Signature Moves
Corrective Therapy - Crossface Sharpshooter -Stolen from Paul Arovnik- The victim is on their back. Kensuke holds up the victim's legs and steps inbetween them. He crosses the victim's legs around the leg which they put through and holds them in place with his left arm. He them steps over, turning the victim over on their stomach. Kensuke leans/crouches back to apply pressure, and at the same time, reaches back with his right arm to apply a one-armed crossface. Black Dragon Smasher - Super Spinning Body Slam (Through Legs) Piledriver -Stolen from Inphino Blitz- Kensuke first applies a front headlock, then rotates and underhooks an arm. At this point, he continues his 180 degree rotation and lifts up the victim as if he is going to give them a body slam. Kensuke positions the victim's head down and drops down to his knees, dropping the victim on their head. Last Caress - Reverse Hurricarana setup flowing into Reverse Gory Special Piledriver -Stolen from Kyle Lamen- Kensuke jumps onto the back of the victim's shoulders. He falls backwards while wrapping his legs around the victim's head. Kensuke then falls backwards, and in the process hooks both of the victim's arms. He lands squarely on his feet, and hefts the victim in the air, so that he is suspending the opponent, upside-down and facing away, by his arms. Kensuke then sits down, driving the opponent headfirst into the mat. The Locust Reign - Hurricarana setup flowing into DDT -Stolen from Neurosis- Kensuke leaps at the victim and locks both of their legs around the victim's head/neck. From there, he pushes up and applies a front face lock on the victim. He then falls straight down, driving the victim's head into the mat. Therapy - Kataha-jime Variant -Stolen From Miyagawa- Kensuke stands behind the victim. He reaches under one of the victim's arms with one hand and places it behind the victim's neck and with his other arm he reaches around under the victim's chin and squeezes across the victim's throat. If needed, he drops to the ground and applies a body scissors as well.

To decide the first ever PURE Jr. Heavyweight Title holder. Another brilliant match in the wings, against two men who sport 'The''s in their name.

tenures.bio:
Wrestling Attire: Mang-A-Hero wears a full body spandex costume with various kanji imprints upon it and various manga and jap pop culture logos or imprints on it. He also wears a set of shoulder pads (Hayabusa style) with additional kanji written upon it and each one having 'Go Go Tokyo' written upon it. He wears a martial arts style bandanna around his head with MAH imprinted on a rising sun upon it. There are holes in the eye, mouth, and hair area for the mask and it's made from tight spandex which hugs our hero. His hair is golden blonde and he has soft blue eyes. Often always smiling. His body is well built muscularly, which fills in his suit real well form his tight abs to his built arms and legs

Ring Entrance: 'Tokyo 6pm' by Angina P. plays, strobes activating about the arena as it flashes from dark blue, to white, to red on beat with the intro to the music. Upon the beat bursting with speed, laserlights of various colors shoot from the back entryway to the ring as Mang-A-Hero emerges, showered within the lights and striking several silly martial arts poses before dashing down to the ring, sliding in and posing atop a turnbuckle with hands extended high in air in a cross, yelling 'GO GO TOKYO' as the fans chant along.

Bio:PCW superstar Rent-A-Hero truly loved his time in the United states, he could not get enough. But something egged him as he wondered, 'What else can a spandex enwrapped hero of my stature accomplish in the world of wrestling?' With that question pondering him....it came to midn upon watching an episode of his beloved Sailor Moon. WHY NOT TRY A HAND A PURO? It certainly was a stretch, the more sports entertainment enfluenced Rent-A-Hero joining a puro group, known well for it's serious style of wrestling. With that known, Rent-A-Hero made it a point to TWEAK and UPGRADE his beloved persona and that he did. He sat down and broke down every manga, martial arts, and fight movie tape possible...learning and delving deep into their culture more than before until he was blurting out foolish Dragonball Z gibberish and not matching his mouth with his words. With that feat accomplished or Kryptonian hero did the last thing he could think of...when in Rome, do what the Romans do....in this case Japan. So he took a costume and altered it until all his manga knowledge was imprinted into his new suit. Now embracing his new style of 'Manga-whoopering' our hero hasset his goals on becoming hero to a whole new group of people who are yet to even BEGIN to realize the wild card that is the newly christened Mang-A-Hero. With his beloved Escalflowne collection, a chinse resteraunt menu(he claims it's a universal translator), and a love for the buisness and a new group of fans..Mang-A-Hero hopes to slay and defeat all the villains who have eluded him in the East, and with his new dedication and upgraded moves, it's a very serious possiblity, even if he is not one to be taken seriously himself! WILL HE MAKE THESE DREAMS COME TRUE?! CAN HE SLAY THE FORCES OF FOILONDERING EVIL?! GO GO TOKYO...AND TUNE IN FOR THE NEXT MANG-A-HERO SHOW!
catchphrases:

"RYOKO RANBU!!! Heeeey, a fireball was supposed to come out!! Videogames sure do false advertise..."
"GO GO TOKYO....AND SIT TIGHT FOR THE NEXT MANG-A-HERO SHOW!!"

tenures.style: Developed as much for flash and flair as it is for damage, The End is an All-Rounder, with high-flyer preference (no brawling, no closed fists, no low blows, no eye rakes, no hair pulls, no biting, etc.). The End is very strong for 225 pounds, routinely lifting and tossing around men he physically shouldn't be able to (up to about 300 pounds, then it gets harder). This combined with his unnatural speed and agility make him a dangerous adversary. The End's blindness has made him modify his offense only to the extent that he does not change the attacks he does, but has turned to chain wrestling, turning one move into another into another, to keep him opponent in one spot and deal with them there.
tenures.finisher: 1) Never Again 2) Forever More — 1) The End hits the One Last Time, then immediately rolls back into a Dragon Sleeper locked in from a Camel Clutch position. 2) The End goes to the apron, and as his opponent tries to stand, The End leaps at him/her with a springboard corkscrew shooting star DDT.
signature_moves: See bio
tenures.bio:
Signature Moves Implosion: Full Nelson Chokeslam {The End lifts his opponent up as high as he can in a full nelson, and at the apex of the lift, drops the opponent's left arm as he twists them to the side, and uses his left arm to spike the opponent down with a chokeslam.} Broken: Apron Running Tiger Driver {The End brings his opponent to a standing position on the apron near a ringpost. He doubles them over and lifts them up in a double-arm powerbomb. The End then runs on the apron to the other side of the apron and jumps off to powerbomb his opponent. He sometimes does the move through a pane of glass, a table, or onto the ring steps.} Wasted Tears: Choking Jumping Fisherman's Buster {The End grabs his opponent in a left-handed choke and cradles the right leg with his right arm. Lifting up, The End jumps back and up into the air, taking his opponent over into a choking Fisherman's Buster that drops them on the back of their neck.} Ripped Away: Double Back-to-Belly Over-the-Shoulder Wristlock Moonsault Stomp {The End grabs his opponent by the wrists so that their arms are over his shoulders with his back to them. He runs to the ropes, turnbuckle, guardwall, or whatever's around and moonsaults off of it, falling down on his opponent's chest with a double stomp while jerking their arms out of their sockets.} Silence: Tornado Inverted DDT {The End grabs his opponent in an upside-down/inverted facelock and jumps up, swings around, and plants the opponent into the mat by the back of their head. This, like many of The End's moves, could potentially be used as a finisher, but he prefers to use it simply to damage and disorient his opponent for further attack.} Chaotic Origins: Powerbomb to Chokeslam Backbreaker {The End lifts his opponent up in a powerbomb, then clutches his opponent by the throat with his right hand while they are on his shoulders, and drives them down onto his knee for a backbreaker.} Empty Horizon: Super Inverted Reverse Full Nelson Iconoclasm {With the opponent sitting on the top rope while he stands on the second rope, The End puts his opponent in an inverted reverse full nelson so that he has the arms hooked while his opponent's stomach is touching his back. The End throws his opponent forward into a bodyslam piledriver variation. Empty Horizon is one of three moves that The End has invented.} Blind Luck: Jumping Ear-Clap Kick {The End jumps up and claps his two feet together over the opponent's ear, disorienting them.} Rushing Waterfall: Asai Stardust Press {With his opponent laying on the floor and him on the apron, The End springboards off the ring ropes for a corkscrew 450 splash.} Vortex Descending: Slingshot 450 Splash {The End uses the ring ropes to slingshot himself into a 450 splash to land on his opponent, laying prone on the ground. The rotation is quick, but the move doesn't have much more impact than a running splash; it's one of those moves more for the crowd than to do damage.} Shared Vertigo: Backflip DDT {The End grabs the opponent's head, and does the DDT as normal, but backflips rather than just falling back to add extra velocity to the move.} Foresight: Leapfrog Headscissors Takedown {The End stands behind his opponent. Using the opponent's shoulders as a sling, he jumps up and over his opponent, catching the head between his feet and rolling the opponent over into a headscissors takedown.} Fall from Grace: Powerbomb Lift to Vertical Superkick {The End lifts his opponent up into a powerbomb, but instead of slamming them to the mat, he releases the opponent and performs a vertical superkick, going between the opponent's legs and hitting them square under the chin.} Chaos Revisited: Sleeper Hold German Suplex {The End locks his opponent in a standing sleeper hold that he throws back into a Sleeper Hold German Suplex, the opponent landing on the back of their head and neck and tumbling onto their stomach.} Cyclotron: 630 Moonsault {The End executes a top rope moonsault that rotates twice, with The End hitting the opponent chest-to-chest. The End lands straight into a pin, but despite the two rotations, the moonsault itself doesn't have much velocity to it. Plain and simple, while the move looks nice and does a little damage, it doesn't have enough impact to win the match. The point of this move is to do some damage, and to make the opponent expend energy and air to kick out of the pin attempt.} Burning Wheel: Somersault Stomp {The End climbs to some elevated position, facing his opponent. He does a full 360 front flip, landing in a double stomp to his opponent's chest or stomach. Only in extreme situations will he execute the double stomp to the head.} Zeta Flip: Corkscrew La Quebrada Moonsault {The End springboards off the middle rope in the ring at an opponent in the ring. He twists laterally in a corkscrew moonsault and lands on his opponent. He does not use this as a pinning move, rather a move that disorients his opponent to leave them open to further attack.} Chasing Dragon: Rope Walk Corkscrew Springboard 180 Turn Dragonrana {The End walks on the ropes, the opponent standing some distance away. When lined up with the opponent parallel to the ropes, The End springs off the ropes, facing away from the opponent, and backflips at him, landing on the opponent's shoulders facing in the same direction as he is. The End spins 180, and takes the opponent over into a Hurricanrana Pin. Again, this move looks nice, but does next to no damage. The move is designed to make the opponent expend energy to kick out of a pin attempt.} Destiny Bond: Moonsault Powerslam {The End takes the opponent into his arms perpendicular to his standing position. The End then springs off of some elevated position and performs a moonsault with the opponent still in hand, landing an impact falling powerslam when both come crashing to the mat; The End laying across his opponent's chest with a lateral press pin. This is the strongest of The End's pinning moves, but once again, it's not designed to win the match, it's designed to get the opponent to waste energy kicking out of it.} Hurtful Uprising: Elevated Powerbomb to Frankensteiner {The most rarely seen move in The End's repertoire. The End lifts his opponent onto his shoulders in a powerbomb position. The End then moves his arms out from under the opponent's legs, clutching the victim's shoulders. The End quickly jumps up to the opponent's shoulders and executes a frankensteiner. The move flows very quickly, and the opponent's feet never touch the floor before the move is completed. The move itself, however, is very complicated and must be done from some elevated area, be it the top rope, the guardwall, or another such place.} Frailty: Running Diving High Angle Shooting Star Press to Outside {With the opponent laying outside on the floor, The End runs off the opposite ropes, charges the opponent, and jumps over the top rope. Falling down on the opponent, The End rotates into a shooting star press, landing chest first across the opponent. This may be done to an opponent set up on a table.} Blackout: Hybrid Submission Mexican Cobra {The End combines a Mexican surfboard with a cobra clutch.} Spiraling into Madness: Super Somersault Ipponzei {The End stands his opponent upon the top rope and he stands on the second rope. The End tosses his opponent down to the mat with an ipponzei shoulder throw, while at the same time somersaulting to the mat. The opponent lands on the mat, while The End simultaneously lands on his opponent, making the damage from the move two-fold. It is still not strong enough to pin the opponent, but The End does it as much for the crowd as he does for damage.} Attack Combinations 40 Days: Attack Combination 1 {Irish Whip Powerslam to spinning kick to the face to standing Shooting Star Press} 40 Nights: Attack Combination 2 {Falling Powerslam to Fallaway Slam to standing Moonsault double knee drop} Broken Promise: Attack Combination 3 {Dragon Suplex to Full Nelson Driver to Surfboard Stretch} Great Crusher Epsilon: Attack Combination 4.0 {Palm thrust to nose, to palm thrust to chest, to Roaring Elbow} Great Crusher Sigma: Attack Combination 4.5 {Thrusting sidekick to knee, to roundhouse kick to stomach, to Corkscrew Backflip Enziguri to doubled over opponent} White Noise: Attack Combination 5 {The End powerbombs his opponent, then lifts the opponent back up and positions him across his shoulders in a fireman carry. The End tosses the opponent's body back while keeping the throat of the opponent underneath his shoulder. The opponent's throat is crushed in by the variation of a samoan neckbreaker. The End then rolls back and locks the opponent in a reverse Boston Crab. The opponent screams in pain, but thanks to the damage from the samoan neckbreaker, makes no sound.} All Alone: Attack Combination 6 {The End grabs his opponent in an upside-down front facelock and executes an elbow smash to then chest/throat of his opponent. The opponent falls, but The End does not. The End then does standing 360 leg drop, and when he lands it he moves straight into a Jujigatame cross arm breaker.} Decay: Attack Combination 7 {Fireman's Carry Gutbuster to Gutwrench DDT to La Magistral Pin} Raging Tsunami: Attack Combination 8 {Sitout Chickenwing Jawbreaker to Chickenwing Inverted Side Russian Legsweep to Chickenwing Crossface w/ Body Scissors} Rigor Mortis: Attack Combination 9 {Tiger Suplex to Inverted Double Arm DDT to Sitting Butterfly Armbar w/ Arm Scissors} Angina: Attack Combination 10 {Cobra Clutch Front Russian Legsweep to Cobra Clutch Slam to Cobra Clutch with Body Scissors} Shocking Rave: Attack Combination 11 {The End executes an Inverted DDT that impacts onto his knee. He keeps the inverted facelock held on and lifts his opponent and spins 180 for a Swinging Falling Inverted DDT. Keeping his opponent in the inverted facelock, The End stands to his feet and lifts the opponent up to into the tombstone position, then cradles the leg and body of his opponent to drop into a Tenzan Driver cradle kneeling tombstone.} Crazy Train: Attack Combination 12 {The End executes a Fisherman Suplex which he chains into a Fisherman Buster that gets chained into a Muscle Buster -- a kneeling Fisherman shoulder-to-shoulder Shoulderbreaker.} Turbo Buster: Attack Combination 13 {This combo is a Snap Suplex chained into a Gargoyle suplex chained into a T-Bone Suplex.} No Escape: Attack Combination 14 {The End chains a German Suplex into Elevated Double Chickenwing Face Drop into a sitting Stretch Plum abdominal stretch chinlock.} Never-Ending: Attack Combination X {This is The End’s longest chain maneuver and something he only bothers to do in EXTREME desperation situations to both damage his opponent and give him time to recover from the attacks that he has suffered. The End first executes an arm wrench hook kick that DOES NOT make his opponent fall to the mat. The End holds to his opponent’s arm and pulls him into a Shortarm Roundhouse Kick. The opponent should now be on the ground, and since The End still holds onto the arm is taken into a Stepover Toehold. That submission is chained into an Inverted STF. When The End drops this submission, he moves right into a Crossface, which is then chained into a Wakigatame armbar. This move is turned into a sitting reverse armbar, and finally chained into a Jujigatame cross armbar.} Counter Attacks Demon Spin: Top Rope Small Package {Only done as a counter to opponents climbing the top rope for a high-risk maneuver facing the ring, The End springs to the top rope and quickly rolls up his opponent while falling back to the mat. The End lands the move in a Small Package Pin.} No Limits: Super Millenium Suplex {Only done as a counter to opponents climbing the top rope for a high-risk maneuver facing away from the ring, The End springs up to the top rope, locks in a standing Crossface Chickenwing, and lifts the opponent up in the submission while dropping it back into a suplex.} Shock Absorber: High Angle Gutwrench Powerbomb to outside {Only done as a counter to opponents standing on the apron who attempt to hit The End with a shoulder block through the top and middle ropes. The End sidesteps slightly, grabbing his opponent in a gutwrench; he pulls them through the ropes, lifting them up to his shoulder, and powerbombs them over the top rope, impacting the floor.} The End Times: Apron Inverted Frankensteiner {Only done as a counter to opponents standing on the apron who attempt to punch or kick The End over the top rope. The End blocks the punch/kick, headbutts his opponent to stun them, then uses the ropes to sling himself onto his opponents shoulders facing the same direction as his opponent. He takes the move back with an inverted Frankensteiner that drops his opponent head-first onto the floor.} Enough: Spinning Sitting Double-Arm Face-First Piledriver {Done only as a counter to an opponent attempting a spear, tackle, or other form of double-leg takedown; The End quickly grabs his opponent in a double-arm standing headscissors, then spins 360 using his own opponent's momentum to lift and carry the move. The End finishes the move in a sitout 'Pedigree' maneuver.} Double-Edged: Rolling Prawn Hold Wheelbarrow Suplex {Done only as a counter to a clothesline, lariat, or other swinging arm attack. The End ducks under the attack, slips behind his opponent, and executes a backflip bridge pin, aka Rolling Prawn Hold. Rather than hold the bridge in a pin, The End rolls out while clutching his opponent by the waist. He pulls up and lifts the opponent back, sending the back of their head crashing to the mat.} Conundrum: Tilt-a-Whirl Tornado Gutbuster {Done only as a counter to some form of dropkick. The End sidesteps slightly and catches his opponent in the dropkick, rotating the opponent's body so that they lay stomach-first on their shoulder. The End then spins 360 before dropping the opponent across his knee stomach-first in a gutbuster.} Fade Away: Chickenwing Cradle Suplex {Done only as a counter to a kick by his opponent, The End cradles the opponent’s leg, moves in close to put his opponent in a chickenwing with his free arm, locks his arms around the lower back of the opponent, and then takes the opponent over with a release suplex.} Zero: Back-to-Belly Cradle Bodyslam Piledriver {Done only as a counter to a kick by his opponent. This is really just a long-winded, fancy name for a cradle suplex variation. The difference is that The End is facing away from his opponent as he cradles the opponent's leg and locks his arms behind his opponent's head. The End throws his opponent forward into a bodyslam piledriver.} Rack of the Damned: Forced Leg Split to Flipover Neck Whip/Running Dropkick {Done only as a counter to a kick by his opponent, The End catches the opponent’s leg and pulls it away from him faster than he can follow, bringing the opponent down into a very uncomfortable front leg-split. While The End could leave it at this, he will follow up by running off the ropes either with a somersault neckbreaker whip, or a dropkick to his opponent’s chest to force them back over onto their back leg, stretching their muscles even farther.} Cracking Up: Stepover Jumping Spinning Roundhouse Kick {Done only as a counter to an opponent's kicking attack. The End catches the kick and brings the leg to stomach level. Stepping over with his left leg, The End jumps while spinning around and hits a Jumping Spinning Roundhouse Kick to the chest with the same left leg.} Wild Fury: Spinning Gory Special DDT {Done only as a counter to an opponent’s punching attack. The End ducks his opponent’s punch while grabbing the hand used to initiate the attack. He spis his opponent around and lifts them up into a a Gory Special crucifix backbreaker submission. The End spins around in the move for a little while before reversing his own momentum, dropping the opponent’s left arm with his right, and spinning into a DDT. The End also invented this move.} Hyper Fire: Belly-to-Belly Armbar Front Facelock to Spinning Falling Facelock Facebreaker {Done only as a counter to an opponent’s punching attack, this is a single attack with two parts. First, The End blocks his opponent’s punch, grabbing the opponent’s arm in a belly-to-belly armbar while moving in close and pulling the opponent down into a front facelock. The End now spins he and his opponent a full 360 degrees while falling to the mat. The End finishes the move by landing the opponent's face into the mat. This move is done in one smooth motion, and is much faster than it sounds. This is the last of three moves The End has invented.} Mark of the Beast: Front Cobra Clutch Palming Headslam {Done only as a counter to an opponent’s punching attack. The End stands in front of his opponent and uses his left arm to place the right arm of his opponent over their nose and mouth, cutting off their breathing. The End then places his right arm across the throat of his opponent, lifts him up high into the air, and drops him to the mat by spiking him headfirst -- palming the opponent by the forehead.} Glazen Stare: Front Pumphandle Sitdown Piledriver {Only done as a counter to a punching attack; The End stands in front of his opponent and puts them in a front facelock with his right hand. With the left hand, he places the opponent's right arm over his neck, and sends his left arm through the legs to be held by The End's left arm. The End lifts up his opponent into the air for a modified suplex, but throws it up and forward into a kneeling piledriver variation.} Comeuppance: Front Handstand Mule Kick {Done only as a counter to an opponent attacking with a chair, stop sign, the steel ringstairs, a pane of glass, or other flat-sided weapon. With the opponent wielding the weapon at face level, The End faces his opponent, lunges forward into a handstand; reaching forward with his legs and giving a front mule kick that sends the weapon into the face of his opponent.} Crash from Below: Backflip Kick {Done only as a counter to an opponent attacking with a chair, stop sign, the steel ringstairs, a pane of glass, or other flat-sided weapon. With the opponent wielding the weapon underneath face level, The End faces his opponent, runs forward, but stops a few steps from his opponent and does a standing moonsault backflip, knocking the chair up into his opponent's face.} The Hard Way: Jumping Double Stomp Face Slam {Done only as a counter to an opponent attacking with a chair, stop sign, the steel ringstairs, a pane of glass, or other flat-sided weapon. With the opponent wielding the weapon above their head, The End kicks the opponent in the gut to double-over the opponent. The End places the weapon on the ground underneath the opponent's face, then grabs the opponent by the hair and pulls them into a standing headscissors. The End does not execute a powerbomb, but instead jumps up and uses both feet to stomp the opponent's face down onto the weapon.} Extinction Level Event (ELE): Weapon-Assisted Cobra Clutch Elevated Face Slam {Done only to an opponent swinging with a bat, pipe, kendo stick, or other two-ended cylindrical weapon. The End evades the weapon attack, grab his opponent's wrist while clutching the weapon while turning around the opponent around with their arm over their face. The opponent should now be in a Cobra Clutch, holding the weapon over the bridge of their nose. The End lifts his opponent up, swings the torso forward, and drops the opponent in a Cobra Clutch Face Slam, the weapon that hits the mat/ground impacting their face for twice the damage.} Lazurus Strike: Weapon-Assisted Tiger Suplex '85 {Done only to an opponent jabbing with a bat, pipe, kendo stick, or other two-ended cylindrical weapon. The End sidesteps the jabbing attack, grabbing the weapon with one hand while spinning behind his opponent. The End puts his opponent in a Half-Nelson Chickenwin with the weapon, and lifts back for a suplex, with the opponent's head impacting the weapon and the mat.}
****Entrance**** The End walks to the ring, with Powerman 5000's 'Bombshell' playing over the speakers. With little in the way of acknowledgement of the fans, The End calmly, very focused, walks out to the ring and jumps up onto the apron. After a high angle springboard landing backflip into the center of the ring to show his agility, The End stretches for his match in his corner.
****Bio**** The End grew up without his parents, they died in a car accident when he was four. He doesn't dwell on it, per se, but he still remembers them fondly. The End's life up to the age of eighteen is hard to follow, due to records being lost. It is believed that he was an orphan in Virginia, USA until that point, but the facility closed under undisclosed circumstances, and nothing but a burnt wreck stands in place of it. Once The End got out of the orphange, he went to college and gained degrees in Biochemistry and Business Administration. He doesn't seem to care much for these fields, he probably just considered it something to do. We don't know how, but it is presumed that at some point he went to Japan. The End says that he did, and saw a Puroresu event. He credits that as being his inspiration to get into the sport of wrestling. The End came back to America, and apparently he gained employment in a garbage federation known as the HWF. We couldn't find many records from it as the federation has been closed for over a year, but we were able to verify his employment in the federation under the name 'Enigma.' This 'Enigma' would later surface in the UWWC, a bigger regional federation. Records from this federation show that The End was its star performer, losing only 3 professional matches, none of which were clean defeats. He is famous for being the only Grand Slam (or as the UWWC referred to him, the 'OmniChampion') Champion in the federation's history. The End changed his name to Seppuku during his tenure in UWWC and continued his rocket to regional stardom. When the UWWC closed last summer, The End came to the PTC looking to make a name for himself. He joined the PWA and within a week was promoted to EW, a developmental organization for PCW. There he won his first PTC title, the Primetanium Title, against a man who had cheated to hold it for eight weeks with a crooked promoter working to keep it on the champion. During his time in EW, The End's employer made the entire roster submit to house-arrest tagging. The End willingly took the house arrest implant, but misinformation resulted in a faultly experimental chip to be implanted in the back of his neck. When The End removed the chip himself, it caused him to go blind. The End's blindness, by all studies and medical reports, is irreversible and he must live with this condition for the rest of his life. The End was faced with a hard choice, to give up wrestling, or to continue and work through his disability, turning it into an advantage. He worked hard, and quickly adjusted to his lack of sight, and within but a few short weeks, The End was fully competent in blind-fighting, and he returned to wrestling ready to regain his lost time in the ring. With his honor code, innovative offense, and disability overcome, The End was one of EW's top stars until the federation was expelled from the PTC. At that point, The End decided to stay with the PTC, and his loyalty and talent paid off as PCW finally accepted him into its roster. The End has been signed with PCW for nearly 8 months now and continues to wrestle there, even winning the Cruiserweight Title in that federation, but The End's one true love has always been Puroresu wrestling, something he hopes to be more involved in now with joining PURE for the second time.

tenures.bio:
Appearance: Akamu is very muscular and powerful. Broad shouldered and barrel chested. His skin is caramel tanned, his eyes almond shaped. He keeps his head shaved clean, as well as his face except for a thick goatee with his upper lip kept clean. His right arm is completely covered in tiger stripe tattoos. On his back he has a tattoo of a black tribal sun encircled by a dragon and a tiger chasing each other's tails. He has a kanji tattoo on each side of his neck, on is the symbol for 'warrior' and the other is 'tiger'. He is chiselled, little body fat and in peak physical condition.

He is a true babyface, he is looking for the honorable fight. He had been in Japan, competing in puroresu for two years before looking to break into the US scene. His path has brought him back to Japan now as he competes in PURE.

In ring attire: Mid thigh length black silk shorts, similar to many kick boxers, with Tiger across the back in gold kanji letters. Black fingerless gloves with wrist supports. He wrestles bare foot, his ankles taped heavily.

After Akamu's birth his mother and father were together for some time, however his father's life in the Corp pulled him away and he didn't want to give his wife and kid the military life. He sent them money and had them stay in Manoa. Akamu grew up an agressive child, he excelled at all physical activities. When he was very young, his mother placed him in judo classes. Akamu fell in love and was soon learning jujitsu as well as karate. Through his training Akamu began to control his temper, and the neighborhood fights ceased. From the age of 8 he trained his arts until he turned 23 and went to Japan to join a small time Puroresu promotion. During middle school and high school Akamu excelled at wrestling and football. After graduation Akamu went to the University of Hawaii and wrestled. He graduated in 1999 at the age of 22 with a degree in philosophy. When Akamu was 18 his father returned home. Akamu shut him out because he felt abandoned, however through wrestling he and his father bounded. His father's advice helped to achieve a record of 67-9 while he was at UH. After graduation Akamu went to japan and hooked up with a puroresu promotion that had toured in Manoa before. It was here that Akamu Day became known as Tiger Akamu because of his ferocious style of combat. Shortly there after Akamu gained his tattoos. He wrestled there for two years. He came back to the states to make a name for himself but his path has brought him back to where he started.
